title: Healthy Habits & Wellness
subtitle: Six things, done most days. That is the whole method.
objectives: Name the main dimensions of wellness
Explain what sleep does for the body and the brain
Explain hydration and why thirst is a late signal
Describe the go, grow and glow food groups
Explain why a habit beats a burst of effort

cards.title: Health is not only whether you are ill
cards.text: The usual definition has several parts, and most of them have nothing to do with disease at all.

cards.title: Four you will be asked about
cards.text: Wellness is usually split into physical, mental, social and spiritual. They pull on each other constantly.

cards.title: What each one actually does
cards.text: Tap through. Every one of these appears somewhere in the quiz.

question.text: Which is a dimension of wellness?
question.explain: Physical, mental, social and spiritual are the four the syllabus uses.

cards.title: The body does its repairs at night
cards.text: Growth hormone is released mostly during deep sleep. Muscle repair and memory filing both happen while you are unconscious.
points: **Memory is sorted overnight**, not during the day.
**Missing sleep is not something you catch up.**

cards.title: You grow while you are asleep
cards.text: That is not a figure of speech. The hormone that drives growth is released in pulses, and the biggest one is at night.
points: **Sleep is when it is rebuilt stronger.**
**Skip the sleep and you keep the damage.**
**The session is only half the work.**

question.text: About how much sleep does an eleven to thirteen year old need?
question.explain: Nine to eleven hours is the usual range. Repair and memory filing both happen in that window.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is water, food and how habits actually form. Get up for a second.

cards.title: Thirst arrives late
cards.text: By the time you feel thirsty, you have usually already lost enough water to slow you down.

cards.title: What it is actually for
cards.text: Water carries nutrients, removes waste and cools you by evaporating off your skin as sweat.
points: **Sweating is a cooling system**, not a fault.
**A humid day** makes sweat evaporate slower.
**That is why humid heat** is more dangerous.

cards.title: Dehydration costs you rounds, not comfort
cards.text: Losing even a small percentage of body water measurably reduces endurance and reaction time before you feel unwell.
points: **Fighters drink to a schedule**, not to thirst.

question.text: Feeling thirsty is an early warning that you need water.
question.explain: It is a late signal. Performance drops before thirst arrives, which is why athletes drink on a schedule.

cards.title: Go, grow and glow
cards.text: The three groups are a simple way to check a plate. Most meals should have something from each.
points: **A plate missing one group** is missing a job.

cards.title: A late session costs you twice
cards.text: Bright light in the evening delays the hormone that makes you sleepy. The game ends and the brain stays switched on.
points: **A bright screen tells your brain** it is still daytime.
**Sleep then starts later**, not shorter by choice.
**Stopping earlier is the cheapest win** on this list.

cards.title: Small and repeated beats big and rare
cards.text: A habit works because it costs you almost no decision. That is the actual mechanism, not willpower.
points: **Attach a new habit** to an existing one.

question.explain: Grow foods are the building materials. Go foods are energy and glow foods are protection.

terms.def: Health across physical, mental, social and spiritual dimensions.
The stage where repair peaks and growth hormone is released.
Losing more water than you take in. Performance drops before thirst.
Energy foods: rice, bread, root crops.
Body-building foods: fish, meat, eggs, beans.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **About nine hours** of sleep at your age.
**Thirst is a late signal.** Drink earlier.

quiz.text: Which four dimensions of wellness does the syllabus use?
quiz.explain: They pull on each other constantly, which is why health is not only about illness.
quiz.objective: Name the main dimensions of wellness

quiz.text: Being free of illness is the same as being well.
quiz.explain: False. Wellness includes mental, social and spiritual dimensions as well as physical health.
quiz.objective: Name the main dimensions of wellness

quiz.text: When is growth hormone mostly released?
quiz.explain: The largest pulse comes at night. Growing while asleep is literally true.
quiz.objective: Explain what sleep does for the body and the brain

quiz.text: What else happens to the brain during sleep?
options: The day's memories are sorted and stored
Nothing at all; the brain shuts off
New muscles are grown in the brain
quiz.explain: Memory filing happens overnight, which is why sleep before a test beats late revision.
quiz.objective: Explain what sleep does for the body and the brain

quiz.text: How much sleep does someone aged eleven to thirteen usually need?
quiz.explain: Nine to eleven hours is the usual guidance for that age.
quiz.objective: Explain what sleep does for the body and the brain

quiz.text: Why is thirst a poor guide to hydration?
options: Performance already drops before thirst is felt
Thirst only happens in hot weather
Thirst means you have drunk too much
Thirst is not a real sensation
quiz.explain: Reaction time slows first, then endurance, and only then do you notice.
quiz.objective: Explain hydration and why thirst is a late signal

quiz.text: How does sweating cool the body?
options: It evaporates off the skin and carries heat away
It lowers the heart rate directly
quiz.explain: This is why humid heat is more dangerous: sweat evaporates more slowly.
quiz.objective: Explain hydration and why thirst is a late signal

quiz.explain: Go foods provide energy. Grow foods build and glow foods protect.
quiz.objective: Describe the go, grow and glow food groups

quiz.explain: They protect the body, mostly through vitamins and minerals.
quiz.objective: Describe the go, grow and glow food groups

quiz.text: A balanced meal should include something from all three food groups.
quiz.explain: True. A plate missing a group is missing a job that group does.
quiz.objective: Describe the go, grow and glow food groups

quiz.text: Why does a habit work better than occasional big effort?
options: It costs almost no decision each time
quiz.explain: Removing the decision is the mechanism. Willpower is what habits let you stop spending.
quiz.objective: Explain why a habit beats a burst of effort

quiz.text: What is a good way to start a new habit?
options: Attach it to something you already do daily
Do it at a different time each day
Start with the hardest possible version
quiz.explain: Same time, same place, attached to an existing routine. Missing one day is fine.
quiz.objective: Explain why a habit beats a burst of effort

teacher.summary: Week 8 covers the Health strand on habits and wellness. The lesson deliberately explains mechanisms rather than issuing instructions: sleep is taught through growth hormone and memory consolidation, hydration through evaporative cooling and the order in which performance degrades. That framing matters for a child who trains — 'drink water' is advice he has heard and ignored, while 'reaction time drops before you feel thirsty' is a reason. The habit card describes habit formation as decision cost rather than willpower, which is both accurate and kinder.
discussion: Ask him what time he would have to be asleep to get nine hours before school.
Ask why humid heat is harder on the body than dry heat at the same temperature.
Ask him to check one recent meal against go, grow and glow, and say what was missing.
Ask which existing daily habit a new one could be attached to.
teacher.extension: Have him track sleep and water for five days on paper, then say which day he trained best and whether the numbers explain it. One page, no app.
misconceptions: 'Health means not being sick.' Wellness has mental, social and spiritual dimensions too.
'You can catch up on sleep at the weekend.' Some recovery happens, but the repair missed on the night is not simply repaid.
'Drink when you are thirsty.' Thirst is a late signal; performance drops before it arrives.
'Habits are about willpower.' They work by removing the decision, which is why the timing and place matter.
